notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: D0 (shared mob registry), D (trial spawners, vaults, lodestones, breezes), W (darkness, vibrations, sculk, warden), E1 and E2 (known limits), F (Elden Ring boss), later M1-M3 (remaining mobs). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL, even where a brief says to: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new enum variants, match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small. Record decisions in the track log. D0 is on the critical path: tracks D, W, M1-M3 and F wait for its registry. Keep each group to its brief section; never touch existing families' behaviour. D0's own generic arms go at the end of each list, as its brief says; the note about related positions is for the other tracks. RESTARTS: if this run was started again after a stop (the PC crashed on 2026-10-28 at 20:27 with six tracks building), the worktree may hold the current group's half-done work as uncommitted or staged changes: read `git status` and `git diff` (and `git diff --cached`) first, keep what is correct, finish the group and commit it; discard only what is broken. If cargo reports invalid or corrupt metadata, a truncated .rlib/.rmeta or a link error on a file that should exist, run `& .\scripts\cargo-slot.ps1 +target=<this track's target> clean -p <crate>` for that crate and build again. LOAD: builds now run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. SINCE d0a: d0a is merged (39654c55) and has been in every release since release 2; D (d1, d2 with breezes), W's w1, M1's m1a (rabbits, polar bears), F's f1 and f2 (Margit), E1 and E2 are merged too and use the registry, and trial spawners spawn registry families (674afcc0). track-d0 was fast-forwarded to minecraft-survival before this run. W's w2 (wardens), F's f3, E2's e2b and E1's e1b review run in parallel in their own worktrees. The worktrees moved to C:\Dev\Soscraft\mc-wt\<track> and the repo to C:\Dev\Soscraft\mashup-crafting; briefs may still name C:\Dev\mc-wt: use the new paths. FLYERS: the flying navigation is for M1's parrots (FlyingMoveControl(10, false), FlyingPathNavigation with no doors and can float) and bees (FlyingMoveControl(20, true), a subclass with no doors, no float, required path length 48 and isStableDestination = the block below is not air, its tick skipped while pollinating), and M3's allays and ghastlings (FlyingMoveControl(180, true), path length 48, can float, no doors, canMoveDirectly = isClearForMovementBetween(.., false)); docs/round10/track-m1.md M1-9 and M1-10 and track-m3.md (FlyingMoveSink, the happy ghast section) say what they expect. Make those settings and overrides possible from a family without editing flying.rs again, and say in the track log whether the flying navigation plugs into MonsterGoalContext.navigation and the brain's MoveSink or stays a GoalExtra piece run after the goal step (the M briefs handle both, but must know which).
